original.target_description: Original primary paper unavailable; terminal acquisition miss recorded for DOI 10.1016/j.euroecorev.2004.01.004. Replication-paper reproductions are secondary sources and were not substituted.

replication.target_description: Relationship between merit goods and private consumption (Column 2, Table 5, augmented by disposable income). Same-period reconstruction (1970–1996), difference-GMM country panel, second numeric column; current private-consumption growth is the dependent variable. The 1996–2015 extension is a separate column and is not combined.

n.location: p. 15, Table 6, Observations row, Replication (1970-1996) column; missing-data discussion pp. 6–8
n.sample_role: Country-year observations in the target regression (12-country OECD panel).
n.exclusions: Unbalanced reconstruction due to unavailable historical observations; exact row-level exclusions are not listed. Disposable-income specifications have 225 observations rather than 232.

es.location: p. 15, Table 6, row Δ𝑚 𝑖,𝑡, column Replication (1970-1996)

p.location: p. 15, Table 6, row Δ𝑚 𝑖,𝑡, column Replication (1970-1996); table significance legend
p.quote: Δ𝑚 𝑖,𝑡                          0.534***                   0.471***                 0.357** ***=0.01, **=0.05. *=0.10 denote two-sided significance levels.

reported_success.quote:
Taken together, I interpret these results as providing strong evidence in confirmation of F&K’s
findings that merit goods and private consumption are complementary.

notes: Original source has a terminal acquisition miss in the shared cache; no original statistics were taken from Song’s reproduced F&K columns. No target-coefficient test statistic is printed: the table prints regression coefficients and Newey–West standard errors, so the printed coefficient is retained without conversion. The J-test chi-square and p concern instrument validity and are not the target test. P is the printed star-defined significance threshold, not an exact p-value. The authors’ success verdict concerns merit-goods results collectively, including both periods; it is not a claim that this individual coefficient passes a particular significance threshold.
